blocks.html: La inspección busca confirmar si hay chinches, dónde están y qué extensión tiene el problema. Con eso se elige el método y se decide el alcance del tratamiento. Forma parte del proceso de control integrado.

blocks.h2: Antes de ir: conversación y fotos por WhatsApp
blocks.html:
Te pregunto cuándo notaste algo por primera vez, si hubo un tratamiento o productos caseros, en qué habitación se duerme y dónde aparecen las picaduras y otros indicios.

Puedes enviar fotos por WhatsApp sin coste para una primera orientación. Una foto permite orientar, pero no sustituye a la inspección y no garantiza un diagnóstico seguro: que no se vea nada en una foto no descarta una infestación, y que sí se vea algo no equivale a un diagnóstico.

blocks.h2: Cómo es la inspección en el lugar
blocks.html:
Reviso estos puntos:

  • colchón y costuras;
  • somier, base de cama y cabecero, desmontando parcialmente la cama si hace falta;
  • muebles cercanos;
  • rodapiés, grietas accesibles y juntas;
  • otras habitaciones cuando el caso lo justifica.

Busco ejemplares vivos, huevos, manchas oscuras de excrementos y mudas, y con ello estimo la gravedad y la extensión. No siempre se documenta con fotos de forma sistemática.

• linterna de mano potente y linterna frontal;
  • lupa;
  • espejo de inspección;
  • herramientas manuales para desmontar parcialmente la cama;
  • trampas de monitorización.

Cada recurso de la web cumple una función distinta: la guía para saber si tienes chinches explica los indicios con detalle, el atlas fotográfico permite compararlos y el identificador orienta sobre el siguiente paso. Esta página describe el servicio, no repite esas guías.
Con lo que se encuentra se define la estrategia: tratamiento químico dirigido, vapor seco o una combinación, según el caso. Una inspección sin hallazgos tampoco descarta por completo una infestación.

items.title: Vapor seco
items.text: Calor localizado, sin insecticida en el paso de vapor.

blocks.html: The inspection aims to confirm whether there are bed bugs, where they are and how far the problem extends. That decides the method and the scope of treatment. It is part of the integrated pest management process.

blocks.h2: Before the visit: conversation and photos by WhatsApp
blocks.html:
I ask when you first noticed something, whether there was a treatment or home remedies, which room is slept in and where the bites and other signs appear.

You can send photos by WhatsApp at no cost for a first orientation. A photo can guide, but it does not replace the inspection and cannot guarantee a certain diagnosis: seeing nothing in a photo does not rule out an infestation, and seeing something is not a diagnosis.

I go through:

  • the mattress and its seams;
  • the bed frame, base and headboard, partly dismantling the bed if needed;
  • nearby furniture;
  • baseboards, accessible cracks and joints;
  • other rooms when the case justifies it.

I look for live insects, eggs, dark spots (excreta) and moults, and use them to estimate severity and extent. It is not always documented systematically with photos.

• a strong hand torch and a head torch;
  • a magnifying glass;
  • an inspection mirror;
  • hand tools to partly dismantle the bed;
  • monitoring traps.

Each resource on this site has a different role: the guide to telling if you have bed bugs explains the signs in detail, the photo atlas lets you compare them and the identifier suggests the next step. This page describes the service and does not repeat those guides.

What is found defines the strategy: targeted chemical treatment, dry steam or a combination, depending on the case. An inspection that finds nothing does not completely rule out an infestation either.

items.title: Chemical treatment
items.text: Targeted application according to the extent.

items.title: Dry steam
items.text: Localised heat, no insecticide in the steam step.

blocks.html: The on-site inspection is part of the treatment that is ordered; it is not offered as a stand-alone service or a separate visit. With private clients I explain the result verbally. That verbal information does not replace any treatment documentation the regulations may require.

faq.q: Can I tell if I have bed bugs from bites alone?
faq.a: No. Bites alone cannot confirm that you have bed bugs, and an inspection that finds nothing does not completely rule out an infestation either. The identification guide explains which signs to look for.

faq.q: Can I book just the inspection?
faq.a: No. The on-site inspection is part of the treatment that is ordered; it is not offered as a stand-alone service.

faq.q: Can I send photos before deciding?
faq.a: Yes, by WhatsApp and at no cost. They give a first orientation but do not replace the inspection.

faq.q: Will I get a written report?
faq.a: With private clients I explain the result verbally. For accommodation and businesses see treatment in holiday accommodation.
